question: At identical pretrained parameters and fixed training batches, does preserving loss-path saves remove at least half the full-gradient error introduced by all-eligible int8 saved tensors?
batch_selection: batch_schedule(8, 24, 2, seed)[0] from the committed training split
compression: Existing SavedActivationCodec eligibility and symmetric per-last-dimension int8 reconstruction; parameter-backed aliases excluded. all_saved_int8 encloses model and CE; model_saved_int8 encloses model forward only, with CE outside hooks.
controls: Identical logits hashes and forward loss across all three policies at each fixed batch.
Model parameter hashes unchanged before and after every backward; no optimizer or training updates.
Finite gradients for all 76 parameter tensors and 14067712 parameter elements.
Compare observed logits gradients to (softmax(logits)-onehot)/128 and record row-sum residuals.
Dense gradients retained as comparison references; report full-vector and per-parameter errors, not model quality.
Dense and model-only logits-gradient relative L2 error versus analytic CE must be at most1e-5; all-saved-int8 discrepancy is measured, not rejected by this fidelity tolerance.
evaluation: No holdout forward or evaluation; shared loader only validates committed split structure and hashes. No optimizer steps, hyperparameter or checkpoint selection.
execution: Three fresh sequential CPU workers; one seed batch and three backward policies per worker.180second comparison-loop cap after model loading; parent subprocess cap300seconds. Timing/memory descriptive only because dense gradient references and logits gradients remain live.
stopping: Reject the comparison if any control fails or a worker exceeds the predeclared budget. Preserve a failed dominance gate and all method results; do not retune.
limitations: Three seed-dependent first batches overlap in training examples and are not independent data samples.
This isolates the hook boundary around CE; normalization saves remain compressed in both int8 arms.
Existing synthetic text and traditional Pythia are diagnostics, not AttnRes or learned depth routing.
No training quality, natural-language generalization, wall-clock efficiency or GPU claim.
